comparator.name: Law in Society
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught full-time programme has ten compulsory 6 EC units in each of years one and two. Year three has 30 EC of open study, three 6 EC Recap courses and a 12 EC thesis. The Recap courses require 36 EC from eight specified legal and thematic units. Thesis entry requires Evaluation Research and 30 EC from specified legal, thematic and Recap units. The current thesis course lists Public Law and Terrorism separately where the regulations combine them typographically. Thesis assessment combines an individual legal and empirical study with a group empirical component and poster. English diagnostic completion or the refresher gates the Diversity grade. Professional and Personal Identity coaching carries no credits. Approved alternative elective or exchange packages are subject to course level and approval rules. Civiel Effect requires a separate Dutch preparatory pathway and a qualifying law master.

questionsApplications.label: How can law and policy evaluation improve responses to global challenges such as migration, security, sustainability and market globalisation?
How should companies and digital platforms be held accountable for environmental harm and for the treatment of workers and consumers?

alternatives.concept: Study public, private, criminal, international and human-rights law alongside social research and political science. Use negotiation, comparative legal reasoning and empirical methods to examine how legal institutions respond to questions about security, markets and global governance. Climate science and sustainability governance help explain the problems that legal responses address.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The legal and social research option combines eight legal courses with quantitative and qualitative research, sociology, psychology, negotiation and international governance. Environmental science and business courses give the legal questions context. A separate sustainability and markets option can study policy, firms and environmental impacts, but lacks a distinct sequence in platform regulation, climate law or evaluation of legal interventions. Adding the same legal core would repeat the primary option without establishing a separate legal focus.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: VU requires a dedicated criminology course on explaining, measuring and responding to crime.
VU studies defamation and assault as specific legal problems.
VU examines diversity within the programme’s legal and social context.
Both develop empirical research design and statistical reasoning. UCR applies these skills in a group research project.
Both connect law to philosophical questions about rights and justice. UCR concentrates on human-rights law and its foundations.
Both use psychology to explain behaviour. UCR focuses on social influence, attitudes and group processes.
VU teaches dedicated legal and security perspectives on terrorism. UCR studies youth resilience and educational prevention.
Both examine law and cross-border markets. UCR focuses on transactions, contracts and digital commerce, while VU also studies public and private actors in the platform economy.
Both study international rules and institutions. UCR covers a range of fields in public international law, with migration as one context.
VU studies migration law and the nation state in a dedicated course.
Both teach qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation. UCR applies these methods in social research.
Both introduce sociological theory and institutions. UCR provides tools for examining identity, inequality and social change.
Both teach negotiation through practice. UCR develops bargaining and strategic analysis, while VU also addresses mediation and dispute resolution.
Both examine ethical and social questions about AI. UCR focuses on fairness, privacy and responsibility, while VU also examines technical approaches and legal uses.
VU applies legal frameworks to climate change. UCR provides climate science and policy context.
VU examines ethical questions that legal professionals face in sustainability work.
VU studies multinationals and legal issues in the platform economy.
VU requires a separate statistics course using SPSS.
VU requires a dedicated course on evaluating interventions.
VU uses Amsterdam as a setting for applied sociolegal sustainability research.
Both develop private-law reasoning through comparative study of property, obligations and liability.
Both examine public law and constitutional institutions. UCR compares legal systems, state power, judicial review and rights.
Both study substantive criminal law and legal reasoning. UCR introduces criminal liability and punishment, while VU integrates prior study in a Recap course.
VU requires a 12 EC thesis that combines legal and empirical research. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the schedule.
VU reserves 30 EC for approved open study.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Law in Society integrates public, private and criminal law with social sciences and empirical inquiry. Security, migration, sustainability and global markets organise study of how legal approaches address societal problems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines substantive law courses with sociology, psychology, research methods and negotiation. VU provides dedicated legal study of migration, terrorism, platform markets and climate change, alongside evaluation research and a compulsory thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC curriculum includes 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC thesis. The Recap courses and thesis have separate entry requirements. Professional and Personal Identity coaching carries no credits.
